title: Hall Mint & Hasegg Castle Hall in Tirol
name: Hall Mint & Hasegg Castle Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Münze Hall at Burg Hasegg: birthplace of the thaler and the modern dollar featuring the roller minting press, Münzerturm tower, and town history.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental ensemble of Burg Hasegg and Münze Hall is situated on the southern edge of the historic old town of Hall in Tirol (Bezirk Innsbruck-Land) at an altitude of approximately 560 metres above sea level. Founded in the 13th century to safeguard salt production, river navigation, and Inntal trade, the stronghold achieved global historical importance when Archduke Sigmund the Rich and Emperor Maximilian I transferred the sovereign mint here from Meran in 1477. As the birthplace of the thaler – from whose name the word dollar was derived – Münze Hall is celebrated as a major milestone in European monetary and currency history.

Roller Minting, Museum & Münzerturm

Inside the medieval fortress, an ultramodern museum transports visitors into the intriguing era of masterly coinage technology. The undisputed centrepiece is the true-to-original reconstruction of the world's first roller minting press dating back to 1567: this mammoth wood-and-iron apparatus replaced laborious manual hammer-striking and revolutionised the mass production of freshly minted coins. Visitors can even strike their own commemorative coin on a historic screw press and take it home as a lucky charm. Following the museum tour, guests climb 204 wooden and stone stairs to the top of the distinctive dodecagonal Münzerturm tower – the iconic landmark of Hall. Once at the summit, a breathtaking panoramic vista unfolds across North Tyrol's largest medieval old town, the Inntal valley, and the Bettelwurf chain of the Karwendel mountains.

Visit & Getting There

Münze Hall and Burg Hasegg are open year-round from Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 17:00 (closed Mondays; last admission at 16:00; reduced Sunday hours from November to March). Admission fees including the Münzerturm (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €11.50, seniors approx. €9.50, children and youths (aged 6 to 16) approx. €7.00, family ticket approx. €24.00. Holders of the Innsbruck Card or the Schatzkarte Hall-Wattens enjoy free admission! Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Hall Mitte); underground parking is available at the Altstadt garage or at Unterer Stadtplatz. By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn to Hall in Tirol station, from where a short five-minute walk through the old town leads directly to the castle gate.

Tips

The museum on the ground floor is step-free and barrier-free; the ascent up the historic Münzerturm involves stairs and is not accessible for wheelchairs. In the castle courtyard, the Burgschenke restaurant serves traditional Tyrolean delicacies. Combine your visit with a leisurely stroll through the picturesque cobbled lanes of Hall's historic centre or explore the nearby mining museum.
